CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DEEPAK ROSHAN ---------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Niraj Kishore, Advocate For the State : Mr. Bhola Nath Ojha, APP  --------
10/ 10.06.2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The instant criminal revision application is directed against the judgment dated 22.07.2003 passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.III, Hazaribagh,
whereby the Cr. Appeal No. 158 of 1990 preferred by the petitioner has been dismissed and the judgment of conviction and order of senctence dated 25.07.1990 in G.R. No. 204 of 1987, T.R. No.
319 of 1990, passed by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Hazaribagh, whereby the petitioner was found guilty for the offence punishable under Section 16 (1) a (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- has been affirmed; whereas another accused namely, Rameshwar Narayan was acquitted from the charge of offence under Section 16 (1) a (1) of the PFA Act.
3.

The prosecution case in brief is that Sri M.N. Mallick, the then Food Inspector Hazaribagh submitted prosecution report duly certified by the Additional Chief Medical Officer, Hazaribagh alleging therein that he visited the Kirana shop of accused persons on 25.09.1986 for inspection and during his inspection he suspected that Arhar Dal and wheat flours are adulterated and not fit for consumption.
As such he collected sample as per rules and sent it to the public analyst who reported vide report No. 2580, dated 05.11.1986 that the Arhar Dal was adulterated.
He requested for prosecution, accordingly the cognizance was taken.
Petitiioners were summoned in pursuance of which they appeared.
Thereafter, a charge for offence under Section 16 (1) a (1) of the P.F.A. Act was Gobind Narayan vs The State Of Jharkhand .....

1 framed against the accused persons on 16.06.1989 for which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
After trial they were convicted by the trial court.
The petitioner also lost in appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner confines his argument on the question of sentence and submits that the petitioner remained in custody for about 65 days and he is aged about 62 years and during entire period of bail, he never misused the privilege of bail, as such the sentence may be modified.
5.
Learned counsel for the State supported the judgment and submits that there is no error in the findings given by the Courts below.
As such, the conviction cannot be set aside.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after going through the impugned judgments including the lower courts records and keeping in mind the limited submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the scope of revisional jurisdiction, I am not inclined to interfere with the finding of the courts below and as such the judgment of conviction passed by the learned trial court and upheld by the learned appellate court is, hereby sustained.
7.

So far as sentence is concerned, it is apparent from record that the incident is of the year 1987 and 35 years have elapsed and the petitioner must have suffered the rigors of litigation for the last 35 years.
Further, petitioner remained in custody for about 65 days and now he is aged about 62 years and during entire period of bail he never misused the privilege of bail.
8. In a situation of this nature, I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the petitioner back to prison.
9. Thus, the sentence passed by the trial court and upheld by the appellate court is hereby modified to the extent that the petitioner is sentenced to undergo for the period already undergone.
10. With the aforesaid observation and modification in sentence only, the instant criminal revision application stands disposed of.
11. The petitioner shall be discharged from the liability of his bail bonds.

12. Let the copy of this order be communicated to the court below.
13. Let the lower court record be sent back to the court concerned forthwith.

(Deepak Roshan, J.) Pramanik/
